To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Arsenic concentrations in the irrigation water and in soil decreased with distance from a shallow tube well (STW), and that the As concentrations of soil and plant were significantly related to Fe, Mn, and P. Arsenic, iron, and manganese concentrations in groundwater from tube wells in 61 upazilas (administrative sub-districts) of Bangladesh were determined.
(1) As concentrations of irrigation water in the STW command area were high and varied with distance from the pumping point.
the As concentration in irrigation water and soil decreased with distance from STW, and the As concentration in rice grain was significantly correlated with that of soil.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatial variability and relationship of As with Fe, Mn, and P.
the spatial distribution of As concentrations in irrigation water, soil, and rice grain, and their relationship with soil Fe, Mn and phosphate.
the spatial variability of As concentrations of water, soil and plants (rice), and their relationship to Fe, Mn and phosphorus in the STW command area.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
As in soil and plants is spatially variable and the variability is related to Fe, Mn and phosphorus.
the spatial variability in soil and plant As is mainly controlled by Fe, Mn, and P, which in turn are influenced by the As concentration of irrigation water.
the spatial distribution of soil and rice grain As is controlled by the spatial distribution of As in the irrigation water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
As concentration of water and soil decreases with distance from the point of STW.
As concentrations in water and soil were high in the vicinity of STW point and the As concentrations in soil were significantly and positively correlated to those of rice grains.
As concentration in soil and plant is spatially variable and is significantly and positively related to Fe, Mn and phosphate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
As concentration in rice grain is significantly correlated with As concentration in irrigation water and soil, and that the correlation is stronger in soil than in water.
As concentration in soil and plants are spatially variable and the concentration of Fe, Mn and phosphorus are not always correlated with As. (c) 2011 Elsevier B.V.
